title: FY 2026 President's Budget - Commodity Futures Trading Commission
summary: The CFTC has submitted its FY 2026 budget request seeking $410.0 million and 650 full-time equivalent (FTE) positions, representing a 12.3% increase over the FY 2025 enacted budget. The document outlines organizational structure, division budgets, and provides statistical tables on regulated entities including SEFs, DCMs, DCOs, FCMs, and SDRs.
key_points: CFTC requests $410.0 million total budget and 650 FTE for FY 2026
FY 2026 request represents a 12.3% increase above FY 2025 enacted budget
Document contains organizational structure and division-level budget breakdowns
Statistical appendices include counts of regulated entities: 26 DCMs, registered DCOs, FCMs, SEFs, SDRs, and provisionally registered swap dealers
Figures show volume of futures and options contracts traded and notional value of swaps
Customer protection fund and margin requirements data included
why_it_matters: This budget document is an internal government administrative filing with no direct market impact. It provides baseline statistical information about CFTC-regulated market infrastructure but does not constitute market-moving policy or guidance. The document is most relevant for understanding CFTC operational capacity and the scale of regulated derivatives markets.
market_structure_context: The document contains supplementary statistical data about U.S. derivatives market structure including: number of designated contract markets (DCMs), swap execution facilities (SEFs), derivatives clearing organizations (DCOs), futures commission merchants (FCMs), swap data repositories (SDRs), and provisionally registered swap dealers. Also includes figures on contract volume traded, notional value of swaps, and margin requirements.
